To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cerebellum is essential for learning and expression of predictive timing and integration.
the TD Model of Pavlovain Reinforcement, with extensions to include temporal uncertainty, provides a mechanism to explain the timing of the CR in classical conditioning protocols.
the cerebellum can learn to predict the imminence and timing of a US and to generate a CR that is a prediction of the US.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of timing in the cerebellar cortex.
a computational approach to understanding how the brain represents the temporal structure of events.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TD model provides a plausible mechanism that can account, at the cellular and circuit level, for the acquisition and performance of CR timing.
the TD model provides a plausible and comprehensive account of the acquisition, retention and performance of conditioned responses.
conditioned responses are timed and integrated in a network of cerebellar neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a simple learning rule, operating in the cerebellar cortex and nuclei, is able to account for CR timing in a wide variety of protocols.
the cerebellar circuitry for classical conditioning of the CR is organized to provide a timing signal for the CR.
a simple model can account for the topological features and timing of CRs in a variety of conditioning protocols.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the TD model can account for the temporal dynamics of conditioned responses and the topological features that reflect the temporal relationships between conditioned stimuli and unconditioned stimulus.
a single learning rule, operating on time-tagged elements, is sufficient to account for the topological features and timing properties of CRs.
the cerebellum is a natural substrate for learning and performance in predictive timing.
